experiment: fp8-KV arm for the FAST (PIPE=1 cp.async) prefill flash — px4 hd512 FULL-attn
gate: microbench: fp8 must be FASTER than bf16 at >= 32k, else STOP
device: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
config: single q-tile (BQ=32) at pos seq_kv-32 (full causal KV), n_head=16, n_kv_head=2, nsplit=12 (~1 block/SM), unit dequant scales, best-of-50
implementation: sub-option (i): raw e4m3 staged via the cp.async ring into uint8 smem tiles (row stride HD+16B), dequant to bf16 scratch after cp_wait, reuse ldmatrix/mma; K-scale post-multiplies the score tile per kv column; V-scale folds into the P fragment
note_12b_vs_26b: the px4 hd512 FULL-attn arm is identical geometry for 12B and 26B (n_head/n_kv_head differ but the KERNEL and its compute-bound character do not); the microbench uses the 26B full-attn geometry as the representative worst case. The NO-GO is a property of the kernel, so it holds for BOTH models — no separate 12B run changes the verdict.
root_cause: bf16 issued-BW (2063..2430 GB/s) exceeds the 1535 GB/s HBM ceiling -> the KV read is L2-served, not HBM-bound. Halving KV bytes (fp8) therefore buys nothing; the fp8 arm only ADDS a per-tile dequant pass + 2 __syncthreads on the QK/P.V critical path (dequant->QK serialization). Matches the kernel's own committed px4/T5 ablation (op_attention.cuh:700): the hd512 prefill is softmax(36%)+QK(21%) COMPUTE-bound, per-tile time flat 8k->128k, NOT DRAM-bound.
consequence: fp8-KV cannot make the FAST prefill flash faster than bf16, so it cannot approach vLLM fp8kv TTFT (26B@128k 5133ms) via this lever. Even option (ii) register-direct convert cannot win: the halved-HBM benefit is ~0 on a compute-bound kernel, so best case is parity, never faster.
gates_not_run: hd256 arm, PIPE=1 _pf_fp8kv dispatch/build, and 12B/26B TTFT ladders were NOT executed — the plan's hard sequence STOPs at the microbench on NO-GO.
